item.title: 'Nina Roza' director: 'I was inspired by a real case of a child painter prodigy'
item.description: The director of a film nominated by Canada for next year's Oscars has told FRANCE 24 she was inspired by stories of a child painter prodigy, as well as the idea of identity and what you leave behind when you change countries. The film "Nina Roza" tells the story of a Bulgarian man who leaves his homeland with his daughter and sets himself up as an art curator in Canada.

item.title: UK’s Burnham on a mission to build public support EU reset
item.description: While he insists it would be unthinkable to rejoin the bloc without another referendum, British PM Andy Burnham has nevertheless reopened the debate over Brexit. After striking a deal that brings the UK and the EU closer on issues including food export control standards, youth mobility and carbon emissions, he's set to discuss the future of the relationship with Brussels in the coming weeks and will present the results of the talks in December. It comes despite criticism from a host of former Conservative prime ministers.

item.title: The French mayors refusing to back presidential candidates
item.description: Tuesday marks the opening in Paris of the 108th Congress of French Mayors, where the presidential race is a contentious issue. Candidates need 500 mayor endorsements to run, yet nearly half of mayors this year say they refuse to endorse anyone. France 2 and Caitlin Brown have more.

item.title: France's femicide orphans: The invisible victims of violence against women
item.description: In France, 111 women were killed by their current or ex-partners in 2025 alone, leaving behind dozens of children. How can they rebuild their lives without their mother? How can they seek help? In this episode of France in Focus, we meet Cloé and Eva-Louise, whose world collapsed when their father brutally murdered their mother. FRANCE 24's Natacha Vesnitch, Olivia Bizot, Clément Di Roma and Aurore Cloé Dupuis report.
